newsitem.title: USA: Clinton begins second term with high popularity.
newsitem.headline: Clinton begins second term with high popularity.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton will begin his second term with the highest approval rating since he came to the White House in 1993, according to a new CNN/USA Today poll released on Thursday.
The survey by the Gallup Organisation showed that 62 percent of those interviewed approved of the way Clinton was handling his job as president.
The numbers were similar to those released on Wednesday by the Pew Research Centre in which Clinton scored a 59 percent approval rating, the highest ever recorded by this particular survey.

Pollster Andrew Kohut said Clinton was enjoying a honeymoon with voters fairly typical for second term presidents. His standing was comparable to President Ronald Reagan's at the time of his second inauguration in 1985.

The CNN/USA Today poll also showed a sharp upswing in satisfaction with the state of the U.S. economy over the past four years. Fifty-eight percent said they were very satisfied or somewhat satisfied, compared with 25 percent in 1993.
The poll of 1,005 adult Americans was conducted Jan. 10-13. It has a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.
